The failing test `testCalendarTimezoneRespected` from `FastDateFormat_PrinterTest` class in Apache Commons Lang3 is testing whether the "z" pattern in `FastDateFormat` respects the timezone of `Calendar` instances passed to format. The test creates a `Calendar` instance with a specific timezone, formats the time using `SimpleDateFormat` with the same pattern and timezone, and compares the expected value with the actual value obtained by formatting the time using `FastDateFormat`.

The bug report describes that the timezone formatting bug in `FastDateFormat` causes it to always print the timezone name of the machine's default timezone, ignoring the timezone set on the calendar. This behavior contradicts the expected behavior where the printed time should respect the calendar's timezone.

Looking at the implementation of `FastDateFormat.getInstance(String)`, it retrieves an instance from a cache based on the input pattern without considering any timezone information. This lack of handling timezone information in `FastDateFormat` is likely the root cause of the bug observed in the failing test.

To fix this issue, the `FastDateFormat.getInstance(String)` method should be modified to support timezone information, ensuring that the timezone specified in the `Calendar` instance is respected during formatting.

Next, I will suggest the location to fix this issue.
```java
org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDateFormat.getInstance(java.lang.String)
```
